raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and elevated PTH levels, along with short stature and enuresis, is consistent with pseudohypoparathyroidism. The presence of brain calcification on head CT also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hypoparathyroidism
rejected.why: Low PTH levels would be expected, but the patient has elevated PTH

rejected.label: Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy
rejected.why: While this condition is related to pseudohypoparathyroidism, the patient's presentation does not specifically suggest Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy

rejected.label: Fahr's disease
rejected.why: Fahr's disease typically presents with bilateral symmetrical calcification of the basal ganglia, but the patient's age and other clinical features do not specifically suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Epilepsy with bilateral occipital calcifications
rejected.why: The patient's brain calcification is not limited to the occipital region, and the clinical features do not specifically suggest this diagnosis

gold: Pseudohypoparathyroidism type Ib (confirmed by genetic testing showing broad GNAS methylation changes with loss of all maternal methylation imprints)
